lines.text: A reaction may be slow even when its products are energetically favourable. A catalyst changes how the reactants reach those products, making a lower energy route available.

A catalyst is a substance that increases reaction rate by providing an alternative mechanism of lower activation energy, and is chemically unchanged at the end. Catalysis is this catalytic increase in rate. At fixed temperature the Boltzmann distribution itself stays the same, the lower activation energy threshold leaves a larger area under the curve to its right, so more particles have sufficient energy to react. On an energy against reaction pathway diagram, show catalysed and uncatalysed paths from the same reactant level to the same product level. The catalysed route has a lower barrier, but the overall enthalpy change is unchanged. Measure a forward barrier from the reactants and a reverse barrier from the products, using the peak of the step specified. Homogeneous catalysis has catalyst and reactants in the same phase, heterogeneous catalysis has them in different phases. A catalyst may enter intermediate steps but is regenerated by the end of the sequence.

Activation energy from eight point two is the threshold to compare with the Boltzmann distribution. Reaction pathway diagrams from five point one show why a changed route can lower that threshold while keeping the same enthalpy change.

Catalyst, alternative mechanism, lower activation energy, unchanged at the end. Fixed temperature Boltzmann curve stays fixed, more particles exceed the lower threshold. Draw both paths with the same endpoints and different peak heights. Homogeneous, same phase, heterogeneous, different phases. On the existing Boltzmann diagram, what changes when a catalyst is added at fixed temperature? Keep the curve fixed, place the lower E a threshold to the left, and compare the areas to the right, the larger area means a greater reacting fraction.
At fixed temperature, explain why adding a catalyst increases the fraction of particles able to react without changing the Boltzmann curve.

At a fixed temperature, what changes when an effective catalyst is added? The Boltzmann curve shifts right. The activation energy threshold becomes lower. The products have lower energy. Every particle gains energy. B The catalyst offers a lower energy mechanism. The distribution and endpoint energies remain the same.

N O and N O two are both present in the lower atmosphere as pollutants. The reaction sequence shows the production of ozone from oxygen in the lower atmosphere. This sequence repeats many times. N O two gas gives N O gas plus O gas. N O gas plus one. two O squared gas gives N O squared gas. O two gas plus O gas gives O three gas. Which statement about this reaction sequence is correct?
Both N O and N O two take part and are regenerated later in the repeating sequence. B misses that N O is regenerated too.

The stoichiometry of a catalysed reaction is shown by the equation below. P gas plus Q gas. R gas plus S liquid. Two experiments are carried out in which the amount of R is measured. The results are shown in the diagram. zero zero amount of R experiment one experiment two time. Which changes in the conditions could explain the results shown? one. A lower pressure was used in experiment two. two. A different catalyst was used in experiment two. three. Product S was continuously removed from the reaction vessel in experiment two.
Lower pressure and a less effective catalyst each reduce the rate in experiment two. Removing liquid S slows the back reaction, so C and D include an incorrect explanation.

The reaction pathway diagram for the catalysed reaction and the uncatalysed reaction between. N two and H two is shown. N two gas plus three H two gas. two N H three gas. Which letter represents the activation energy for the first step in the decomposition of N H three in the presence of a catalyst?
For decomposition, measure the first catalysed barrier from the N H three starting level to the first peak, D. B measures from the synthesis side.

The reversible reaction between methanol and ethanoic acid liquids is catalysed by adding a small volume of concentrated sulfuric acid. Two statements about this reaction are listed. one. The sulfuric acid is a homogeneous catalyst. two. The sulfuric acid lowers the activation energy of the reverse reaction. Which statements are correct?
Sulfuric acid and the liquid reactants share a phase, so catalysis is homogeneous. An alternative pathway lowers activation energy for both directions, B omits the reverse effect.

Photochromic glass, used for sunglasses, darkens when exposed to bright light and becomes more transparent again when the light is less bright. The darkness of the glass is due to the presence of silver atoms. The following reactions are involved. reaction one. silver plus plus chloride. silver plus chlorine reaction two. copper plus plus chlorine gives copper two plus plus chloride reaction three. copper two plus plus silver gives copper plus plus silver plus. Which statement about these reactions is correct?
copper plus and copper two plus are regenerated across the reaction sequence. In reaction two copper plus loses an electron, so B incorrectly calls it an oxidising agent.

The Boltzmann distribution for a mixture of gases capable of reaction is shown. The two curves represent the mixture of gases at twenty five degrees Celsius and at thirty five degrees Celsius. The activation energies for the catalysed and uncatalysed reactions are shown. energy number of particles. zero. zero. E a catalysed. E a uncatalysed w x z y. Which row is correct? number of particles with enough energy to react at twenty five degrees Celsius in the catalysed reaction number of particles with enough energy to react at thirty five degrees Celsius in the uncatalysed reaction.
The regions above the catalysed threshold give y plus z for the first condition and x plus z for the second. C omits the additional x region.

The diagram shows the Boltzmann distribution of energies for a reactant gas. For a particular reaction, the activation energy is X. zero. zero energy, E number of particles with energy, E. X. Which change to the diagram occurs if an effective catalyst is added at the same temperature?
An effective catalyst decreases activation energy at fixed temperature. A incorrectly claims that molecular energies increase.

The diagram shows the Boltzmann distribution of energies in a gas. The gas undergoes a reaction with an activation energy, E a. The peak of the distribution is labelled P. zero. zero. E a molecular energy, E proportion of molecules with energy E. P. If the same reaction is carried out in the presence of a catalyst, which statement is correct?
At fixed temperature the distribution peak is unchanged, lower activation energy moves the threshold left. A incorrectly lowers the peak.

The gaseous compound Z decomposes on heating. In the diagram, Boltzmann distributions for Z at two different temperatures, P and Q, are shown. The lines X and Y indicate activation energies for the decomposition of Z with and without a catalyst. zero. zero molecular energy number of molecules. X. Y. P. Q. Which curve and which line describe the decomposition of Z at a higher temperature and with a catalyst present? higher temperature catalyst present.
The higher temperature curve is Q and the lower, catalysed activation energy line is X. D selects the higher barrier.

Gas Q decomposes slowly at room temperature. Q gas gives X gas plus Z gas. The Boltzmann distribution curve for gas Q at room temperature is shown. energy number of particles. E a. zero. zero. Which change occurs when a catalyst is added to gas Q?
Lower activation energy increases the number of particles above the reaction threshold. D moves the threshold in the wrong direction.

The Boltzmann distribution for the hydrogenation of an alkene at a particular temperature in the absence of a catalyst is shown. molecular energy E proportion of molecules with energy E. E a. zero. zero. Which row correctly describes the effects of adding a nickel catalyst to the reaction vessel? the shape of the. Boltzmann distribution activation energy, E a.
Nickel lowers activation energy while the fixed temperature Boltzmann distribution remains unchanged. A incorrectly changes its shape.
Which row is an example of heterogeneous catalysis? reaction catalyst.
The Contact process uses solid vanadium of V oxide with gaseous reactants, so it is heterogeneous. ay has catalyst and reactants in the same liquid phase.

A catalysed reaction pathway has reactants at forty kilojoules per mole, products at ten kilojoules m o l to the power of minus one and a first peak at seventy five kilojoules per mole. Calculate the forward activation energy.
Subtract the reactant energy from the peak, seventy five minus forty equals thirty five kilojoules per mole.
Identify the starting energy level.
Use the peak on the relevant pathway.
Subtract the reactant level from the first peak.
Sketch energy against reaction pathway for an exothermic reaction, with and without an effective catalyst. Label the forward activation energies and the enthalpy change.
An alternative lower energy path joins the same energy levels, enthalpy change is unchanged.
Begin with the axes and endpoint energies.
Add two different paths between the endpoints.
Measure each forward barrier from reactants.

Vanadium and pepsin can both act as catalysts. Vanadium is a metal. Pepsin is an enzyme. Which statements are correct for both vanadium and pepsin? one. They will speed up any chemical reaction. two. They can lower the activation energy for a reaction. three. They are not used up when they act as catalysts.

E a molecular energy, E proportion of molecules with energy E. P. If the same reaction is carried out in the presence of a catalyst, which statement is correct?

Nitrogen oxides are removed from the exhaust gases of internal combustion engines by the action of a catalyst in a catalytic converter. Which row is correct? change in oxidation number of nitrogen type of catalyst.

An autocatalytic reaction is a reaction in which one of the products catalyses the reaction. Which curve would be obtained if the rate of an autocatalytic reaction is plotted against time? rate time. zero zero.

An autocatalytic reaction is a reaction in which one of the products catalyses the reaction. Which curve would be obtained if the rate of an autocatalytic reaction is plotted against time? rate time. zero zero.
Which statement about catalysts is correct?

Disaccharides are hydrolysed in slightly acidic solutions. This reaction is very slow. A biological catalyst is added to a slightly acidic mixture of three disaccharides, sucrose, maltose and lactose. The hydrolysis reaction remains slow for sucrose and maltose but is now much faster for lactose. Which statements about the catalyst are correct? one. The catalyst increases the activation energy of all three hydrolysis reactions. two. The catalyst shows specificity. three. The hydrolysis of lactose using a catalyst has a different mechanism to the hydrolysis of lactose without a catalyst.

A large amount of N two O gas decomposes into nitrogen gas and oxygen gas in the presence of a tiny amount of a gold foil catalyst. The gold foil provides a solid surface on which the catalysed reaction takes place. The graph shows the concentration of N two O gas against time as it decomposes. The graph is a straight line. concentration of N two O gas. zero. zero. ten time or min. Which row describes, the change in rate of reaction as N two O gas decomposes from zero to ten minutes the effect of adding more gold foil catalyst on the rate of decomposition of the same amount and concentration of N two O gas? change in rate of reaction as. N two O gas decomposes effect of adding more gold foil on the rate of decomposition.

The diagram shows the Boltzmann distribution of energies in a gas. The gas can take part in a reaction with an activation energy, E a. The gas is maintained at a constant temperature. Which statement is correct?

At constant temperature, adding a catalyst does not change the Boltzmann distribution, so peak P stays the same. A catalyst provides an alternative reaction mechanism with a lower activation energy, moving the E a threshold to the left and increasing the proportion of molecules with sufficient energy to react. ay and B incorrectly lower the peak, B and D incorrectly move E a to the right.

A gas reacts slowly at a fixed temperature. Explain, using the Boltzmann distribution, why adding an effective catalyst increases its initial reaction rate. Refer to the curve, the activation energy threshold and the area representing particles able to react.

At fixed temperature, the catalyst changes the mechanism and lowers E a, without changing particle energies or the distribution. The larger area beyond the lower threshold represents a larger reacting fraction and hence a higher frequency of successful collisions.
Identify the condition held constant in this experiment.
Consider the distribution curve and the reaction threshold separately.
Begin by linking the stated temperature condition to the spread of particle energies.

Two identical samples of a reactant gas initially have the same temperature. Sample H is heated without a catalyst, sample C receives an effective catalyst while its temperature stays fixed. Compare their Boltzmann plots with the initial plot and explain why both changes increase the initial reaction rate. Assume equal numbers of reactant particles when comparing the plots and no change of mechanism on heating.

Heating changes the distribution, giving more particles energy above an unchanged E a. Catalysis at fixed temperature keeps the distribution unchanged but lowers E a, both increase the reacting fraction, while equal particle numbers give equal total areas.
Organise the comparison into curve shape, threshold position and areas.
Ask which change alters particle energies and which alters the reaction mechanism.
For sample H, first relate temperature to average kinetic energy.

A two step catalysed pathway from R to P passes through these levels in order, R at twenty, first peak X at eighty five, intermediate I at thirty five, second peak Y at one hundred, and P at fifty five. All energies are in kilojoules per mole relative to the same reference. Analyse this pathway, part a, identify the starting level and peak for the first step in each direction, R to P and P to R, and give each barrier, part b, determine whether the forward reaction is endothermic or exothermic, using its enthalpy change.

The first peak encountered depends on the direction, X from R, but Y from P. Subtract the starting level from that peak for each first step barrier, the higher product level gives a positive overall enthalpy change.
Trace the stated sequence in each direction.
For each first step, pair its starting level with the first peak encountered.
Write a peak minus start expression before inserting energies.
eight point three Homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts.
In one breath.

A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by offering a different mechanism with a lower activation energy. At a fixed temperature, more particles have enough energy to react, although their energy distribution has not changed.
Key ideas.

A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative reaction mechanism of lower activation energy, and is chemically unchanged at the end. Catalysis is the increase in rate caused by this alternative mechanism. A catalyst can participate in intermediate steps, being consumed in one step does not mean it is used up overall. Check whether it is regenerated later in the sequence.

Activation energy, E a, is the minimum energy needed for a reaction to occur. On a reaction pathway diagram, measure the forward activation energy vertically from the reactant energy level to the relevant peak. For the reverse reaction, start at the product energy level. A catalyst can lower both forward and reverse activation energies. It does not alter the energies of the reactants or products, so the overall enthalpy change remains the same. It also does not change the equilibrium position.

The Boltzmann distribution describes how particle energies are spread at a stated temperature. Adding a catalyst at that same temperature leaves the shape and peak of the distribution unchanged. Its lower E a threshold lies further left on the energy axis. The area under the curve to the right of that threshold is larger, a greater proportion of particles has enough energy to react. This explains a greater frequency of successful collisions and a faster reaction.

In homogeneous catalysis, the catalyst and reactants are in the same phase. Concentrated sulfuric acid in a liquid esterification mixture is an example. In heterogeneous catalysis, they are in different phases. Solid vanadium of V oxide catalysing the reaction of gaseous sulfur dioxide and oxygen in the Contact process is an example, reaction takes place at the catalyst surface. State the phases when classifying a catalyst, rather than relying on its name.
Method.
Mark the reactant and product energy levels on axes labelled energy and reaction pathway. Their difference is the enthalpy change, which stays fixed with a catalyst.
Draw the uncatalysed pathway with a higher peak and the catalysed pathway with a lower peak. A multi step catalysed pathway may have more than one peak.
Measure each activation energy from the starting level of the direction requested to its relevant peak. In a multi step pathway, the first step ends at the first peak.
On a Boltzmann diagram at fixed temperature, retain the same curve. Move only the activation energy line left and compare areas to its right.
Worked example.

Reactants are at forty kilojoules per mole, products at ten kilojoules per mole, and the first catalysed peak is at seventy five kilojoules per mole. Calculate the forward activation energy. Start at the reactant level because the question asks for the forward reaction. E a equals seventy five minus forty equals thirty five kilojoules per mole. The reverse first step barrier would instead be measured from the level at which that reverse step starts.
Traps.
Trap, The catalyst shifts the Boltzmann curve. Why it's wrong, Temperature, not catalysis, determines that curve. Instead, Shift the E a threshold to the left.
Trap, Measure decomposition activation energy from the synthesis reactants. Why it's wrong, Decomposition starts at the synthesis products. Instead, Identify the stated direction first.
Trap, A catalyst changes reaction enthalpy. Why it's wrong, Both pathways share the same endpoints. Instead, Keep delta H identical.
Exam technique.

For explain, link the alternative mechanism, lower activation energy, larger fraction of particles above the threshold, and increased rate. For sketch, label both axes, endpoints, peaks, barriers and enthalpy change. For a catalyst cycle, follow all steps before deciding which species are regenerated. For homogeneous or heterogeneous catalysis, explicitly compare phases.
